story.titleZh: 2027年F1赛历公布：冲刺赛扩容引发争议
story.summaryZh: The 比赛团队评论F1公布的2027年赛历，指出其中包含令人意外的选择，尤其针对冲刺赛场次扩大至10场以及部分举办地点的选择。
story.originalTitle: Sacrilege? Our verdict on 2027 F1 calendar + sprint expansion
story.summaryEn: The Race team comments on Formula 1's 2027 calendar announcement, pointing out surprising choices, especially the expansion to 10 sprint races and the selection of some sprint-hosting venues.
detailZh: F1的2027年赛历公布比大多数时候更受期待，尤其是考虑到中东地区的不确定性可能仍会扰乱当前赛季的尾声。
因此，虽然看到巴林（萨基尔）和沙特阿拉伯暂时回到赛历上并不令人意外，但纳入10场冲刺赛却令人侧目——其中一些冲刺赛举办地的选择也是如此。
赛季揭幕战——无论是在巴林还是澳大利亚——真的应该附带一场冲刺赛吗？在摩纳哥举办冲刺赛有任何逻辑吗？更多的冲刺赛是否意味着更多的娱乐？
当Edd Straw指出这意味着我们将在那些街道上进行两场排位赛，并且只带着一节练习赛就投入其中时，我对摩纳哥冲刺周末的困惑和恼怒大大减少了。
实际上，这让我更期待摩纳哥周末了（可悲的是，我现在对摩纳哥大多无动于衷）。摩纳哥的冲刺赛很可能是一场糟糕的比赛，但正赛也会如此。摩纳哥已经不再关乎赛车，所以我不太在意。
更过分的是在赛季揭幕战安排冲刺赛。这是亵渎。所有的兴奋、所有的铺垫、所有的期待——我们却把它浪费在对主赛事的肤浅模仿上？
原则上我对冲刺赛没意见，2027年它们不可避免的扩张也没问题，即使我希望他们走得更远，提供一些不同的东西，让它们的存在比‘比看FP3好’更有意义。
但这是对一年中最大赛车时刻之一的亵渎。即使是一场精彩的冲刺赛也只是一场冲刺赛。而且它将消除揭幕大奖赛的一项基本乐趣，因为它将不再是年度第一场比赛。
起初，我无法忽视在摩纳哥决定举办一场甚至不需要进站的额外比赛的荒谬性。
然后，当我意识到这也意味着摩纳哥将有两场排位赛时，我想，为什么不干脆更进一步呢？
冲刺赛本身将是浪费时间。你可以把它变成一场到第一个弯道出口的比赛，然后在爬坡途中挥动方格旗。或者如果必须的话，也许跑一整圈并宣布结果。
那么为什么不干脆取消它，改为第三节排位赛呢？
周五的‘冲刺’排位赛可以为周六上午举行的一场一次性对决排位赛设定顺序，并支付冲刺积分。如果你在周五最快，你就有优势在周六最后一个跑。
比起一场冲刺游行，我更愿意看那个——而且还有积分可争。
更多的冲刺赛并不能解决其大问题
冲刺赛场次的增加早已不可避免，但令人沮丧的是F1从未完全致力于该赛制的潜力。
到目前为止，冲刺赛一直是浓缩版的、单次进站的大奖赛，几乎没有自己的个性。迄今为止已有29场冲刺赛，我想知道一位典型的F1车迷会记得其中多少场具体的比赛，就它们产生的比赛而言？
这突显了一个事实：冲刺赛是一次性的、零食大小版本的主赛事，而不是本身独特的东西。
引用的论点是冲刺赛比FP3更有趣，这是正确的。然而，真正的问题是F1是否充分利用了冲刺赛，使它们拥有自己的特色，成为具有自身身份和形态的必看节目，而不是作为主赛事的附属节目。
答案在于需要对该赛制不那么保守。这并不意味着把它变成一场抽奖比赛，或者用荒谬的随机元素来装饰它只是为了制造故事情节，而是考虑重新定义挑战的方法。例如，为什么排位赛必须是现有三段式赛制的浓缩版？
只要核心奇观仍然是尽可能快地完成一圈，就有无数种方法可以使其更加独特。比赛也是如此。只要你在公平公正的基础上进行这些比赛，没有引入随机元素的噱头，这就是创造不同奇观和竞争挑战的机会。
是时候让周末的冲刺赛元素拥有自己的特色和身份，使它们成为必看节目，真正增加体育挑战，并以不同方式测试车队和车手。
冲刺赛制实际上可能让摩纳哥变得混乱
当我第一次看到摩纳哥被列入2027年冲刺赛日程时，我的第一反应是这太疯狂了！
在F1第二难超车的赛道（你好，马德里赛道）上举办冲刺赛可能有什么好处？
但我想得越多，就越能看到尝试它的逻辑——因为它可能让整个摩纳哥大奖赛周末本身变得有点疯狂。
是的，周六的冲刺赛可能不会达到戏剧性的顶峰，但由此产生的时间表调整意味着大量F1需要更多的东西：危机感。
车手在排位赛前调整自己和赛车的两节练习赛将不复存在。
现在他们只有周五上午的那一节练习赛，然后就直接投入——在一个排位赛几乎决定一切的地方争夺冲刺赛发车位。
在冲刺赛中排在第一位将有很多利害关系——包括更多的冠军积分。然后第二天他们必须再次出发。
那些在周五下午搞砸的人会在周六犯同样的错误吗？周六和周日发车位之间是否会出现一些迷人的变数？
人们常说摩纳哥大奖赛最精彩的部分是排位赛。明年我们将得到两次。
我非常期待看到这一切如何发展……
detailEn: Formula 1's 2027 calendar announcement carried more anticipation than most tend to, particularly considering the uncertainty in the Middle East that may still disrupt the back end of the current season.

So while it's no real surprise to see Bahrain (at Sakhir) and Saudi Arabia back on the calendar for now, the move to incorporate 10 sprints is eyebrow-raising - as is the choice of some of those sprint-hosting venues.
Should the season opener - be it in Bahrain or Australia - really have a sprint attached? Is there any logic to a sprint race in Monaco? And do more sprints translate to more entertainment?

I became far less baffled and annoyed by a Monaco sprint weekend when Edd Straw pointed out that it means we will get two qualifying sessions on those streets, and go piling into them with just a single practice session.

Actually, it makes me look forward to the Monaco weekend more (I am sadly largely ambivalent to Monaco nowadays). In all likelihood, Monaco's sprint will be a bad race, but so will the grand prix. Monaco's not about racing anymore, so I don't really care.

What's far more egregious is having a season-opening sprint race. It's sacrilege. All the excitement, all the build-up, all the anticipation - and we burn it on a shallow impersonation of the main event?

I'm fine with the sprints in principle, and the inevitable expansion of them for 2027, even if I wish they went further and offered something different so they had a more meaningful existence than 'it's better than watching FP3'.

But this is a desecration of one of the biggest racing moments of the year. Even a great sprint race is just a sprint race. And it will eliminate a fundamental joy of the opening grand prix because it will no longer be the first race of the year.
At first I couldn't look past the absurdity of deciding to have an extra race that doesn't even feature a pitstop around Monaco.
Then, when it dawned on me that it also means two qualifying sessions in Monaco, I thought, why stop there?

The sprint itself will be a waste of time. You could make it a race to the exit of the first corner, then drop the chequered flag on the run up the hill. Or if we must, then maybe do a whole lap and declare the result.
So why not bin it off entirely and have a third qualifying session?

The Friday 'sprint' quali can set the order for a one-shot showdown session that takes place on Saturday morning and pays the sprint points. If you're fastest on Friday, you get the advantage of running last on Saturday.
I'd much rather watch that - with points on the line - than a sprint procession.
More sprints doesn't solve their big problem
The increase in the number of sprints has long-since been inevitable, but what's frustrating is F1 never fully committing to the potential of the format.

So far, sprints have been condensed, single-stint versions of grands prix with little individual character of their own. There have been 29 sprints so far, and I wonder how many specific ones would be remembered by a typical F1 fan in terms of the race they produced?
This underlines the fact that the sprints are disposable, snack-sized versions of the main event rather than something distinct in themselves.

The argument cited is that sprints are more interesting than FP3, and this is correct. However, the real question is whether F1 has made the most of the sprints in terms of making them have their own character, must-see viewing with their own identity and shape rather than acting as shoulder programming to the main event.

The answer lies in the need to be less conservative with the format. This doesn't mean turn it into a lottery race, or garnish it with absurd random elements just to create a story line, but consider ways to redefine the challenge. For example, why must the qualifying session be a condensed version of the existing three-segment format?

As long as the core spectacle remains completing a lap as fast as possible, there are a plethora of ways this could be made more distinct. The same applies to the race. Provided you run these on a fair and equitable basis without gimmicks that introduce random elements, it's an opportunity to create a different kind of spectacle and competitive challenge.

It's time to give the sprint elements of the weekend their own character and identity and make them must-see viewing in a way that genuinely adds to the sporting challenge and tests teams and drivers in different ways.
Sprint format could actually make Monaco chaotic
When I first spotted Monaco's inclusion on the sprint schedule for 2027, my immediate reaction was it was nuts!
What benefit could there possibly be in hosting a sprint on F1's second-most difficult (hello Madring) track to overtake on?
But the more I've thought about it, the more I can see the logic in giving it a go - because it could make the entire Monaco GP weekend itself a bit bonkers.
Yes, the sprint race on Saturday is probably not going to be peak drama but the resulting shake-up to the timetable means plenty of something that F1 needs a bit more of: jeopardy.
The two practice sessions for drivers to dial themselves and their cars in prior to qualifying will be gone.
Now they have just that single practice session on Friday morning and then they are into it - shooting it out for sprint grid positions in a place where qualifying is almost everything.
There will be a lot on the line - including more championship points - in ending up first on the grid for the sprint. Then the day after they must go again.
Will those that mess it up on Friday afternoon make the same error on Saturday? Is there going to be a fascinating bit of variability between Saturday and Sunday grids?
It is often said that the best part of the Monaco GP is qualifying. Next year we are going to get it twice.
I am quite looking forward to seeing how it all plays out...
keyPointsZh: 2027年赛历中巴林和沙特阿拉伯暂时保留，但中东地区的不确定性可能仍会影响当前赛季尾声。
The 比赛团队质疑赛季揭幕战是否应设冲刺赛，以及摩纳哥冲刺赛的合理性。
团队认为冲刺赛数量增加并未解决其缺乏独特性的根本问题。
keyPointsEn: Bahrain and Saudi Arabia are temporarily retained on the 2027 calendar, but uncertainty in the Middle East may still disrupt the end of the current season.
The Race team questions whether the season opener should have a sprint and the logic of a Monaco sprint.
The team argues that more sprints do not solve the fundamental problem of the format lacking distinct character.

relatedItems.originalTitle: F1 2026 Qatar Grand Prix qualifying results
detailZh: 乔治·拉塞尔夺得杆位，梅赛德斯车队在卡塔尔大奖赛排位赛中占据领先，这是自5月份加拿大大奖赛以来的首次。
以下是排位赛三部分的全部结果：

19 安东内利·阿隆索 (阿斯顿·马丁) +0.436秒

relatedItems.titleZh: 安东内利与梅赛德斯包揽卡塔尔大奖赛练习赛
relatedItems.summaryZh: 基米·安东内利在卡塔尔大奖赛FP3练习赛中连续三次夺冠，梅赛德斯竞争对手似乎在争夺最佳非梅赛德斯车队，红牛在第三次练习赛中取得第三名。
relatedItems.originalTitle: Antonelli and Mercedes sweep Qatar GP practice
detailZh: 基米·安东内利在卡塔尔大奖赛FP3练习赛中连续三次夺冠，梅赛德斯竞争对手似乎在争夺最佳非梅赛德斯车队，红牛在第三次练习赛中取得第三名。
在排位赛前的20分钟内，练习赛中的圈数非常少。似乎很少有车手能在他们的第一次排位赛中取得更好的成绩。
安东内利的队友乔治·拉塞尔在第二阶段的表现中保持了领先，尽管他在著名的14号弯角发生了一次打滑，那里的地板损坏总是令人担忧，这使安东内利得以缩小到落后0.017秒。
但在第三次尝试中，安东内利全速前进，逆转了排名，领先拉塞尔0.249秒，这个成绩无人能及。
梅赛德斯的车手在任何时刻都落后了半秒左右，红牛车队的马克斯·维斯塔潘在练习结束时排名第三，落后安东内利0.510秒。
维斯塔潘的队友伊萨克·哈德贾排名第四，领先略有提升的法拉利车手查尔斯·勒克莱尔，勒克莱尔在周五的比赛中表现不佳，非常悲观。
勒克莱尔的队友刘易斯·汉密尔顿排名第九，抱怨赛车转向不足，并要求增加前翼角度以避免提前进站。
奥斯卡·皮亚斯蒂在最后一次性能测试跑之前排名第三，但在第六和第七位时被麦凯轮车队的兰多·诺里斯超越，最终排名下降。
皮亚斯特里是众多抱怨转向不足的车手之一。
小红牛在周五表现得非常乐观，并在FP3练习中领跑中游，Arvid Lindblad排名第八，劳森排名第十，领先其中游对手两十分。
阿尔派恩落后小红牛很多，小红牛在车队积分榜上领先Enstone车队27分，争夺第五名。加斯利在FP3练习中排名第14，队友科拉平托排名第16。
科拉平托在最后阶段幸运地避开了高速移动的斯特罗尔，这一事件将在练习结束后进行调查。
在劳森和加斯利之间是奥迪和哈斯车队的奥利·贝尔曼，他的队友拉斐尔·卡马拉排名第15。
费尔南多·阿隆索超越了两辆威廉姆斯赛车，为阿斯顿·马丁赢得了第17名。
凯迪拉克车队以瓦尔特里·博塔斯领先近0.7秒的成绩，排在最后一名塞尔吉奥·佩雷斯之前。
第17名 费尔南多·阿隆索（阿斯顿·马丁）+2.696秒
detailEn: Kimi Antonelli completed a hat-trick of practice sweeps in FP3 for the Qatar Grand Prix, as Mercedes' rivals appear to be fighting for the best of the rest with Red Bull taking that honour in third practice.
Very few laps were turned in the first 20 minutes or so, before qualifying runs. It appeared that few drivers could improve on their first qualifying efforts.

Antonelli's team-mate George Russell set the early pace and maintained that lead after the second performance runs despite a wide moment through the notorious Turn 14 - where floor damage is always a worry - and that allowed Antonelli to close in to just 0.017s behind.
But on the third attempts, Antonelli turned on the afterburners to flip the order and lead Russell by 0.249s, which would not be beaten.
Mercedes' challengers were regularly around half a second down at any given point, with Red Bull's Max Verstappen taking third at the end of the session, 0.510s adrift of Antonelli.
Verstappen's team-mate Isack Hadjar took fourth ahead of the slightly improved Ferrari of Charles Leclerc, who was very pessimistic after Friday's running.
Leclerc's team-mate Lewis Hamilton was down in ninth, complaining that the car was not turning in sufficiently and asking for more front wing angle to avoid understeer.
Oscar Piastri had been third before the last performance run attempt, but was jumped by McLaren team-mate Lando Norris as they ran sixth and seventh, shuffled down the order by the end.
Piastri was another of the many drivers complaining of understeer.
Racing Bulls was extremely bullish on Friday and did head the midfield in FP3 with Arvid Lindblad in eighth and Liam Lawson in 10th, two tenths clear of its midfield rivals.

Alpine was well behind Racing Bulls, which is 27 points ahead of the Enstone team in the chase for fifth in the constructors' standings. Pierre Gasly finished 14th and team-mate Franco Colapinto 16th in FP3.
Colapinto was lucky to avoid a slow-moving Lance Stroll at high speed in the closing stages and that incident will be investigated after the session.
Between Lawson and Gasly were the Audis and Haas driver Ollie Bearman, whose team-mate Rafael Camara finished 15th.
Fernando Alonso cleared both Williams to take 17th for Aston Martin.
Cadillac anchored the order with Valtteri Bottas nearly 0.7s ahead of last-place Sergio Perez.
17 Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin) +2.696s
keyPointsZh: 梅赛德斯竞争对手在练习赛中落后梅赛德斯约半秒。
keyPointsEn: Mercedes' challengers were around half a second behind at any given point.

relatedItems.titleZh: 韩泰启动F1轮胎测试并接触车队，准备竞标2029年供应合同
relatedItems.summaryZh: 韩泰已启动F1轮胎测试计划并与车队展开谈判，准备竞标从2029年起成为F1官方轮胎供应商。F1当前与倍耐力的合同持续到2028年底。
relatedItems.originalTitle: Hankook emerges with serious F1 tyre supply push
relatedItems.summaryEn: Hankook has begun a Formula 1 tyre testing programme and opened talks with teams as it prepares to bid to become the official F1 tyre supplier from 2029. F1's current contract with Pirelli runs until the end of 2028.
detailZh: 据The Race了解，韩泰已启动一项F1轮胎测试计划，并与车队展开谈判，为竞标从2029年起成为大奖赛官方供应商做准备。
F1目前与倍耐力的合同持续到2028年底。此前，这家意大利公司击败普利司通的竞争性报价，赢得了F1最近一次招标合同，覆盖2025至2027年。
今年6月，在国际汽联行使选择权后，其合同又延长了一个赛季。
然而，从2029年起，国际汽联将启动新的招标程序，届时似乎将出现新的竞争，以争夺F1官方供应商资格。
据了解，倍耐力希望先等待看到招标细节，然后再决定是否参与竞标，以延长其自2011年以来的当前合约期，而普利司通长期以来一直在评估重返F1的可能性，其代表已出席过多场比赛。
然而，现在有消息显示，韩泰也准备加入竞争，并且一直在暗中加大自身的努力。
该公司的代表被发现出现在最近的拉斯维加斯大奖赛上，据了解，这是他们继9月前往马德里之后，今年第二次造访F1比赛。
据The Race了解，韩泰利用这些行程会见了大多数车队，并与老板、首席执行官和其他高级管理人员讨论了计划。
然而，前往各地观看比赛——其中还包括2025年在中国、日本和新加坡举行的赛事——只是其为2029年做准备的努力的一方面。
据了解，韩泰已在公司内部组建了一支44人的专项工作组，为进入F1做准备。
除了投入研发能力和模拟器运行之外，该公司今年还使用一辆改装的F2同级测试车完成了两次F1轮胎开发测试，以评估潜在的轮胎结构以及不同配方。
第三次测试已安排用于研发其雨地轮胎，该公司希望这也能帮助其开发出一款具有更窄水雾羽流的轮胎，以减少湿地条件下造成的能见度问题。
韩泰也在努力进行生产和制造规划，以满足任何轮胎招标合同下供应F1、F2和F3轮胎所需。
韩泰对国际汽联的赛事当然并不陌生，这家韩国公司已经是世界拉力锦标赛的官方轮胎供应商，并且刚刚结束了对电动方程式锦标赛的供应，而普利司通将在即将到来的赛季接替。今年早些时候，韩泰还被指定为该管理机构的全球合作伙伴。
2029年之后的新F1轮胎招标期几乎肯定会涵盖向下一个规则时代的过渡，F1正着眼于更轻、更灵活的新赛车，以配合从2030年开始改用V8动力单元。
这些计划还将包括一种新的轮胎设计，该设计将比目前的18英寸设计略微减小车轮尺寸。
detailEn: Hankook has begun a Formula 1 tyre testing programme and opened talks with teams as it prepares to bid on becoming grand prix racing’s official supplier from 2029, The Race has learned.

F1’s current contract with Pirelli runs until the end of 2028, after the Italian company won F1’s most recent tender deal, which covered the period from 2025-2027, against a rival bid from Bridgestone.
Its contract was extended by a further season in June this year after an option was taken up by the FIA.
From 2029, however, a new tender process is set to be launched by the FIA and there looks set to be fresh competition to secure the right to be the official F1 supplier.

It is understood that Pirelli wants to wait to see details of the tender before deciding if it enters the fray to extend its current spell which stretches back to 2011, while Bridgestone has long evaluated an F1 return with representatives having attended races.
However, it has now emerged that Hankook is ready to throw its hat into the ring too and has been secretly ramping up its own efforts.
Representatives of the company were spotted at the recent Las Vegas Grand Prix, which was understood to have been their second visit to an F1 race this year following a trip to Madrid in September.
The Race understands that Hankook has used these trips to meet a majority of teams and discuss plans with bosses, CEOs and other senior executives.
The trips to races, which also included visits to events in China, Japan and Singapore in 2025, are only one side of its efforts to get ready for 2029, however.
It is understood that Hankook has already committed a 44-person task force within the company to prepare for an F1 entry.

Beyond committing research and development capability plus simulator running, it has this year completed two development tests for F1 rubber using a modified F2-equivalent-mule car to evaluate potential construction as well as different compounds.

A third test has been scheduled to work on its wet-weather rubber, which it hopes can also help it develop a tyre that features a narrower spray plume to reduce visibility problems caused in wet conditions.
Hankook is also working hard on production and manufacturing planning that would be required to supply F1, F2 and F3 tyres that would come under the umbrella of any tyre tender contract.

Hankook is certainly no stranger to FIA competition, with the South Korean company already the official tyre supplier to the World Rally Championship and has just ended its supply to Formula E where Bridgestone is taking over for the upcoming season. Earlier this year Hankook was also named as a global partner of the governing body.

The period of the new F1 tyre tender beyond 2029 will almost certainly cover the transition to the next rules era, with F1 setting sights on new lighter and nimbler cars to coincide with the switch to V8 power units from 2030.
The plans are also set to include a new tyre design, which is set to reduce wheel size slightly from the current 18-inch design.
keyPointsZh: 倍耐力在击败普利司通的竞争性报价后赢得2025至2027年的F1轮胎供应合同，今年6月国际汽联行使选择权将合同延长一个赛季。
国际汽联将从2029年起启动新的招标程序，届时预计将出现新的竞争以争夺F1官方供应商资格。
